story: In the early hours of 3 January, US forces raided Caracas and carried Nicolás Maduro to New York to face drug charges. On 28 February, the US and Israel went to war with Iran and killed its supreme leader. In between and since, the administration imposed 50 percent tariffs on Canada, its closest ally, and hosted the World Cup. Few years have shown so plainly how much one American president can reshape the world without asking Congress first. Americans now get their first chance to answer at the ballot box.

The midterm elections are on 3 November, and the mood is bleak for the president's party. An NPR/PBS/Marist poll in September put Trump's approval at 39 percent, with 53 percent strongly disapproving, the highest share since the question was first asked in 2017; 45 percent of voters said their vote for Congress was a vote against him (NPR via WGCU). A Reuters/Ipsos poll this month put him at 32 percent, and he has been campaigning in normally safe Republican areas of Texas (ABC News). Trump told Republicans at an unprecedented midterm convention in Dallas to "pretend that I'm on the ballot," while some Republican candidates have begun breaking with him on key issues. If Democrats take the House, the second half of Trump's term will look very different: subpoenas, blocked bills and possibly impeachment.
briefing.power: A federal presidential republic. The president is elected indirectly through the Electoral College for four years, with a two-term limit. Congress has a 100-member Senate and a 435-member House, all of whose seats and a third of the Senate's are up every two years. The Supreme Court and the 50 states share power under the Constitution.
briefing.holders: President Donald Trump (Republican); Republicans control both chambers of Congress until at least January 2027.
